scope: Root-owned composition, runtime, provider application ports, Jobs read seams, HTTP routing/auth/header/query validation, backup sanitation and Database transaction tuning; listed integration/lifecycle/backup/DB test diffs. Adjacent B/C constructors and ownership helpers only traced to evaluate these seams; not an independent full B/C review. Own DTO/frontend implementation excluded except readback of root query fix.
observations: Factory selects explicit empty source/proof registries and side-effect-free secret/transport objects. Only lifespan initializes DB/secrets, recovers abandoned dispatches and starts worker; supplied native lifecycle test separates live lease skip, expired lease unknown terminal, and repeat recovery. Production source and model proof remain absent.

HTTP reuses authenticated SessionIdentity, write Origin/CSRF, no-store response, strict typed bodies, unknown/duplicate query rejection, raw single command keys and quoted lowercase strong config If-Match. Current protected Policy and immutable ACK replay are service-owned, exercised through real HTTP tests; root router does not fabricate authorization or expose request/secret bytes.
Runtime configuration readiness uses Provider-owned metadata; it does not equate secret_present/configured with successful auth or remote capability.
Jobs seams inspect actual workspace-owned kind and strict current lease in caller transaction, without writing owner job state or substituting fabricated generation jobs.

Backup verifies distinct physical copy and owned histories, excludes locators/private HMAC references, preserves immutable facts and checks a separate dispatch-disabled digest projection. Export remains explicitly sensitive; full M7 restore remains NOT_RUN. Live original and online migration backups are distinguished.

Database timeout accepts strict bounded integers and preserves existing defaults; deferred transaction is opt-in. Actual fixture exercises committed-read visibility and bounded lock failure without replacing cancellation guarantees.
